name: High-Energy Hook Then Rest Beat
use_when: A short starts with dense motion, text, overlays, SFX, or fast cuts.
The hook uses a designed text sequence that needs a cleaner body structure afterward.
The editor needs high energy without exhausting the viewer.
The hook is visually intense but the rest of the explanation needs comprehension.
The short uses a simple dynamic zoom/proof hook, then needs a slower human body without losing momentum.
avoid_when: The format is a calm talking-head clip where intensity would feel fake.
The target style intentionally stays maximalist from start to finish.
The rest beat would create dead air instead of comprehension.

timeline_pattern.energy_rule: Put maximum energy into the hook, then reduce visual density briefly so the viewer can process the point.
timeline_pattern.rest_rule: A rest beat can be a clean talking-head shot, simple tracking shot, or quieter B-roll as long as it keeps momentum.
timeline_pattern.body_rule: After the hook, rotate through the lightest useful body support: simple talking head, filler card, B-roll text, or full-screen animation.
timeline_pattern.return_rule: Re-introduce zooms, overlays, or SFX on important statements, not on every sentence.
timeline_pattern.slow_human_rule: After the hook, slower human moments can work when they create connection, proof, or emotional clarity rather than empty space.

motion.rule: Use less motion after the hook until the next claim, proof, or transition needs emphasis.
motion.dynamic_zoom_note: A long simple dynamic zoom can be enough for an emotional body section if the face/story already carries attention.

sound.rule: Reduce SFX density after the hook so speech stays clear; bring back hits or whooshes on meaningful movement.

captions.rule: Keep captions readable during the rest beat and avoid stacking them with extra title text.

color.rule: High-energy color or overlay effects should not make the rest beat feel like an accidental style break.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render hook and post-hook sections separately to compare visual density. Use contact sheets to check whether the rest beat still has a clear focal point.
implementation.remotion: Tag sections as hookIntensity, restBeat, accentBeat, or payoff; reduce overlay and SFX components during restBeat sections.
implementation.blender: Reserve heavier animated elements for hook and accent beats, then use simpler camera or text movement for rest sections.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: After a dense hook, use a clean clip with light tracking before adding the next preset-heavy motion sequence.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers for hook, rest, body visual, accent, and payoff; toggle adjustment layers and SFX groups to compare density.

common_mistakes: Keeping hook-level intensity for the whole short until the viewer cannot process the point.
Adding a rest beat that becomes empty dead air.
Cutting out a human imperfection that would have made the post-hook section feel warmer.
Using effects on every sentence instead of the important statements.
Treating filler cards, B-roll text, and full-screen animations as equal-weight effects instead of choosing by line importance.
Dropping energy so hard after the hook that the short feels unfinished.
qc: Does the hook feel energetic without making the claim unclear?
Does the post-hook rest beat preserve momentum?
Does any slower post-hook section have a named connection, proof, emotion, or comprehension purpose?
Are effects reintroduced on important statements rather than every sentence?
Can the viewer understand the explanation after the dense hook?
Does SFX density drop enough for speech to stay clear?
Are body visuals chosen by line importance rather than applied on a fixed schedule?
